goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

It does not show (or change) any Salesforce client construction logic, token refresh behavior, unconditional refresh calls, or credential write/update paths at/around the referenced line. adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — Concurrent first-time webhook deliveries can both pass findFirst and race create, producing duplicate credentials or a non-idempotent server error.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler implements a check-then-act flow: it does `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and, if none is found, it calls `prisma.credential.create(...)`. This is not atomic. Two concurrent first-time webhook requests for the same (userId, appSlug/appId) can both observe “no credential” and both proceed to `create`. If there is no unique constraint, duplicates can be created; if there is a unique constraint, one request will fail with a DB uniqueness error (yielding a non-idempotent 500 unless caught). Nothing in the diff adds locking/upsert or error handling to make this race-safe, so the finding describes a real issue in the introduced code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — If sharing is enabled while the webhook secret is unset, an omitted header equals undefined and unauthenticated credential replacement is accepted.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler authenticates by checking `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset (i.e., `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is `undefined`) and the request omits the header (so the header lookup also yields `undefined`), the comparison becomes `undefined !== undefined` which is false, so the request is accepted and proceeds to decrypt and upsert credentials. This is a verifiable auth bypass in the diff when sharing is enabled but the secret is not configured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync fetch has no timeout, so an unresponsive integration endpoint can indefinitely stall every token-dependent calendar operation.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, when credential sync is enabled it performs `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` without any AbortController/timeout signal. This function is now used in multiple token-refresh paths (e.g., Google/Office365/Hubspot/Lark), so if the configured sync endpoint is slow or never responds, the awaited fetch can block those token-refresh operations indefinitely (at least until underlying network/socket timeouts), stalling token-dependent calendar operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84 — Lark requires the provider's nested `data.data` envelope although the new sync contract promises only an access token and expiry.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. When syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` response (per its comment: “response should only contain the access token and expiry date”). But immediately after, Lark code does `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`, which is a Lark-specific response parser for the Lark provider refresh endpoint response shape. There is no adaptation layer (unlike Google/Office365 which add `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) to handle the different sync response contract, so the sync response is likely to fail parsing/handling in Lark’s `handleLarkError` path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod keys are literal string properties rather than an arbitrary numeric expiry field, so an ordinary access-token-plus-expiry response cannot satisfy the advertised sync contract.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed object keys like `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()`. In JS this evaluates to a single literal property name (whatever `z.string().toString()` returns, e.g. "[object Object]"), not “any string key whose value is a number”. Zod `z.object({...})` also doesn’t support arbitrary additional keys this way; the second computed key similarly becomes another literal key and can overwrite/duplicate. As a result, a normal token response such as `{ access_token: "...", expiry_date: 123 }` will not satisfy this schema, breaking the intended "access token + numeric expiry" sync contract when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is on.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — Missing refresh tokens are replaced by the literal sentinel string `"refresh_token"`, which office365calendar merges into the credential and saves (CalendarService.ts:264-272), overwriting the real refresh token so later refreshes send `refresh_token=refresh_token` and fail forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — The sync branch returns a Fetch Response with no `data`, then swallows the resulting refresh failure and continues with expired credentials.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes, a concrete bug is visible in the diff. In `GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, the code now does:

```ts
const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...);
const token = res?.data;
```

But `refreshOAuthTokens()` returns a `fetch()` `Response` object when the sync branch is taken (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`). A Fetch `Response` does not have a `.data` property (that’s typical of axios). The additional claim that it "swallows the resulting refresh failure and continues with expired credentials" is not directly verifiable from the shown diff (the catch/handling behavior isn’t included), but the core issue (sync branch returning a Response without `.data` and breaking refresh) is real and introduced here.

So under `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && credential.userId`, `hubspotRefreshToken` will actually be a Fetch `Response`, not a parsed `HubspotToken` (no `.json()` parsing occurs). adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:26 — The secret check compares a possibly-absent request header to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` with `!==`, so when the env var is unset both sides are `undefined` and any unauthenticated caller passes the check and can write OAuth credentials for an arbitrary userId.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — The webhook secret is compared with a non-constant-time `!==` string comparison rather than `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, leaking prefix-match information through response timing.

adjudication.rationale:
In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the webhook authentication check does a direct strict-inequality comparison:

```ts
req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
```

This is a normal JS string (or string[]) comparison, not a constant-time comparison. For verifying a secret, this can leak information via timing (e.g., faster failure on length/prefix mismatch vs later mismatch), whereas `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (after normalizing to Buffers of equal length) is the standard mitigation. The issue is directly present in the diff and is a reasonable security finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — The decrypted payload is `JSON.parse`d and written verbatim into `credential.key` with no schema validation, so any JSON value (a bare string, an unrelated app's key shape, or attacker-tampered CBC ciphertext output) is persisted as a user's app credential and later blind-cast to a token type by the integrations.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler decrypts `reqBody.keys` and immediately does `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`, then writes `key: keys` into `prisma.credential.update/create` with no validation of the decrypted JSON’s shape/type against the expected credential schema for the given `appSlug`. This is directly visible in the diff. As a result, any JSON value that successfully parses (object, array, string, etc.) will be persisted into `credential.key`, while other parts of the codebase (shown in the diff) commonly treat `credential.key` as a specific token/credential type via casts (e.g., `credential.key as ...` in multiple integrations), making this a real correctness/safety issue. The specific mention of “CBC ciphertext output” is speculative about the crypto implementation, but the lack of schema validation and verbatim persistence is real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:58 — process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` defaults to an empty string instead of failing closed, so a self-hoster who enables credential sharing without setting the key gets an unhandled decrypt exception per request rather than a clear refusal.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, decryption is performed with `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` and the result is immediately `JSON.parse(...)`’d, with no guard/validation that `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set and no try/catch. The `.env.example` also documents the key “must be 32 bytes”, but the code will proceed with an empty string if it’s missing, which will very plausibly cause `symmetricDecrypt` and/or `JSON.parse` to throw and return a 500/unhandled exception rather than a clear “misconfigured/forbidden” response. That’s a concrete defect introduced by the diff (fail-open on missing key and no graceful error handling).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The outbound POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no secret, bearer token, or signature, so the sync endpoint this establishes as the reference pattern must return any user's live OAuth access token to any caller that can reach it; the response is also used without checking `response.ok`.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it performs `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no auth material (no secret header, bearer token, signature, etc.) and no other verification. That is directly verifiable in the diff and means the sync endpoint has no application-provided way to authenticate/authorize the request beyond implicit network trust. Also, the function returns the raw `fetch` response without checking `response.ok`, so non-2xx responses will flow to callers unchecked (some callers then proceed to parse/use the response).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5 — Both computed keys in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` evaluate to the same literal string `"[object Object]"` (the second overwriting the first), so once credential sharing is on the app-specific schema is discarded for one that validates only `access_token`, and the unauthenticated sync endpoint's response is stored into `credential.key` essentially unvalidated.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `minimumTokenResponseSchema` the computed property names use `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()`. `z.string()` returns a Zod schema object, so calling `.toString()` on it yields a plain string (typically `"[object Object]"`), meaning both computed keys collapse to the same literal property name and the latter overwrites the former. As a result, the schema effectively requires only `access_token` and does not enforce any numeric “expiry” field as intended. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` selects this weakened schema instead of the app-specific `schema`, so token responses are validated far less strictly than intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — A missing refresh token is silently replaced with the literal string `"refresh_token"`, which office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 merges over the stored credential and persists, destroying the user's real refresh token and permanently breaking that connection.
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same core bug: when the OAuth refresh response lacks a refresh_token, the code substitutes the literal string "refresh_token", which overwrites/persists over the real stored refresh token and breaks future refresh/authentication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — No handler test covers an unset webhook secret, which makes a missing request header authenticate because both values are undefined.

adjudication.rationale:
In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the auth check is:

```ts
if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
  return 403
```

If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is **unset** (i.e., `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET === undefined`) and the request also omits the header (so `req.headers[...] === undefined`), the comparison becomes `undefined !== undefined` which is `false`, so the request is treated as authenticated and proceeds. That is a real fail-open condition introduced by this diff (assuming `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true).

The claim about missing test coverage isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the underlying security/correctness issue (unset secret allows bypass) is verifiable in the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — No test exercises the enabled sync branch, so its raw Response return breaks Google Calendar's expected `{data}` response shape at googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `refreshOAuthTokens` when sync is enabled it returns the raw result of `fetch(...)`, i.e. a WHATWG `Response` object (no `.data` property). But `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` uses the returned value as if it were a Gaxios/axios-style response: `const token = res?.data;` and then `token.access_token` / `token.expiry_date`. If the sync branch runs, `res.data` is `undefined`, so `token.access_token` will throw (or at minimum set invalid credentials). This is a concrete response-shape mismatch introduced by the diff; the mention of “no test exercises it” is ancillary/speculative, but the breakage itself is verifiable from the code.
